# WebSocket

A WebSocket, from `nf.http.websocket`: `send` text on it, and hear its `open`, each `message` and its one `end` as events. It belongs to the script that opened it and ends with reason `"unloaded"` when that script unloads (a reload, the server stopping). Once it has ended its methods answer as an ended socket does rather than erroring. Ephemeral: it can't be saved in a `data()` table.

A handle: call its methods with a colon, `websocket:method()`.


## Methods {#methods}

### `websocket:url()` {#url}

The URL it was opened with, even after it has ended.

**Returns** `string`

### `websocket:state()` {#state}

`"connecting"` until its `open` event, then `"open"`, and `"ended"` once its `end` event has been heard.

**Returns** `"connecting"\|"open"\|"ended"`

### `websocket:protocol()` {#protocol}

The subprotocol the other side chose from `options.protocols`, while it's open; `nil` before and after, or when it chose none.

**Returns** `string?`

### `websocket:send(text)` {#send}

Sends a text message. Before the socket opens it waits and goes, in order, once it does. A message over `connections.max-message-bytes` is an error at the script's line; one past the package's `connections.bytes-per-minute` ends the socket (reason `"limit"`) instead of going.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `string` | The message, as text (UTF-8). |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when the socket has ended (or just ended over the limit), so nothing was sent.

```lua
socket:send(nf.json.encode({ op = 1, d = sequence }))
```

### `websocket:close(code?, reason?)` {#close}

Ends it now, with reason `"closed"`: the other side is told with `code` and `reason`, and messages that arrived but weren't handed over yet are thrown away.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code` (optional) | `integer` | The close code: `1000` (a normal close, the default) or one from `3000` to `4999`, which applications define. |
| `reason` (optional) | `string` | Why, for the other side to read: at most 123 bytes. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when it had already ended.

## Events

What `websocket:on(event, handler)` listens for. See [Events](events.md) for how events work.

| Event | Payload | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | [WebSocketOpenEvent](types.md#websocketopenevent) | The connection is made and ready. What `send` sent before it goes now, in order. Heard at most once, never after `end`. |
| `message` | [WebSocketMessageEvent](types.md#websocketmessageevent) | A text message arrived. Messages come in order, on the main thread, a limited number a tick per socket (`connections.messages-per-tick`); while scripts haven't taken them, at most `connections.max-queued-messages` wait and the server stops reading from the network, so nothing is ever dropped. A binary message isn't taken: the socket is closed (code `1003`) and ends `"failed"`. |
| `end` | [WebSocketEndEvent](types.md#websocketendevent) | The socket ended, for any reason (`event.reason` says which): heard once, after every message that arrived before it, while the handle still answers. After it, every handler on the socket is gone. Opening a new socket is how to reconnect. |

### `websocket:on(event, handler, options?)` {#on}

Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `event` | `WebSocket.Event` | The event's name. |
| `handler` | `fun(event: `[`Event`](types.md#event)`)` | Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`. |
| `options` (optional) | [`EventOptions`](types.md#eventoptions) | How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`. |

**Returns** [`Subscription`](subscription.md): Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

```lua
local socket = nf.http.websocket({ url = "wss://chat.example.com/live" })
socket:on("message", function(event)
  log("said:", event.data)
end)
```

### `websocket:once(event, handler)` {#once}

Like `socket:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `event` | `WebSocket.Event` | The event's name. |
| `handler` | `fun(event: `[`Event`](types.md#event)`)` | Called with the event. |

**Returns** [`Subscription`](subscription.md): Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.
